reasons: The opinion text states the under-color rule for misuse of state-conferred power by officials.
The lake treatment scope_note says the under-color definition remains governing and was adopted for § 1983 in Monroe v. Pape, supporting the Section 1983 anchor role.
residual_risks: The home-role label is editorial, but it is supported by disclosed lake judgment fields and the opinion's color-of-law holding.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Keep clear that Classic itself construed the criminal civil-rights statutes; the § 1983 role is by later adoption.

reasons: Opinion paragraph 30 supports the stated proposition: misuse of power possessed by virtue of state law and enabled by state-law authority is action under color of state law.
The same paragraph says the officials acted while performing Louisiana statutory duties to count, record, and certify ballots.
The lake scope_note supports the later § 1983 application through Monroe v. Pape.
residual_risks: The frontmatter holding paraphrases rather than quotes the exact sentence, but the paraphrase does not materially broaden the rule.
